headline: A Stanford team's 'virtual biotech' run by 37,000 AI agents found that drugs aimed at genes active in only a few cell types tend to do better in trials.
score_reason: Interesting research method with real numbers, but a past-records link with no lab test.
importance_line: It may help drug developers pick safer, more promising targets before a trial starts, but it is a statistical link in past trial records that no lab experiment has yet tested.
summary: Earth.com reports that researchers at Stanford, led by James Zou, built a 'virtual biotech' in which an AI agent acting as chief science officer directed 37,075 specialist agents that read trial records in about six hours. They found that drugs aimed at genes active in only a few cell types were 40% more likely to move from phase 1 to phase 2 testing and had 32% fewer side effects reported, but the team stresses this is a link in past trials, not proof, and the agents ran no lab experiments.
notes: Read via AOL copy of Earth.com text; credited to Earth.com. Original earth.com URL not found, AOL link kept.
